newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Pipe plan marks first dent in Dutch gas monopoly.
newsitem.headline: Pipe plan marks first dent in Dutch gas monopoly.

text.p: Dutch utility distributor Delta Nutsbedrijven said on Friday it plans to build a gas pipeline to provide consumers in the southern Netherlands with cheaper gas from Britain and break Gasunie's monopoly of Dutch gas supply.
"Until now there has been no other gas available for Dutch consumers," said Henk Jansen, head of general affairs at Delta told Reuters.
Delta's pipeline will run for about 50 kms from Zalzate on the Belgian border to Ossendrecht in the southern Dutch region of Brabant.
By tapping into the Belgian network, Delta will form a link with the Interconnector pipeline to the U.K. and bring the prospect of cheaper British gas.
The pipeline is due for completion in 1998 to coincide with the start-up of the Interconnector.
The Dutch government still has to formally approve the proposed pipeline, but there are few problems expected.
"It should be passed within a week or so. If so, it will mark the first time two gas pipelines will go the same way," said a spokeswoman at the ministry of economic affairs.

Gasunie, currently the monopoly supplier of gas to distribution companies in the Netherlands, also aims to import gas from Britain via the Interconnector and has plans to build its own pipeline along the same route.
"We are also interested in Interconnector gas and also plan a pipeline from Belgium," said a Gasunie spokesman.

The Interconnector gas pipeline will connect Bacton on the English east coast with Zeebrugge in Belgium and is due to come on stream in October 1998, bringing up to 20 billion cubic metres (bcm) a year of gas from the U.K. to continental Europe.
